title: Why You Can't Cheat in My MMO
author: TheED5
selftext: Every online game gets cheaters: speed hacks, teleporting, infinite gold. So when I built my own MMO engine, MMO Studio, I gave it one rule. The player's computer is never trusted.

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
...so, you are proposing to solve the issue of online cheating by doing client-side simulation of all players at the same time?

hm, this doesn't seem like it could possibly have any flaws 

gee whiz i wonder why nobody has thought of that before

replies.author: TheED5
replies.body: no it's not running the sim for all players at all times! Depending on the how you have your game setup maps can have a population type. if it's a pvp area we cap how many people can enter the map and que them up to join in or they can pass through the zone. in towns people close to you are running 20 tick, mid range 10 far 5 and really far off. And a lot of other things.

replies.author: -svde-
replies.body:
i would ask you what the fuck you’re even trying to say but i know you have no balls ass idea so it’s pointless 

just because you asked the llm a completely incoherent question and asked if it was possible   
and it strained its little brain trying to parse it and came up with something remotely tangible, whatever you *think* is happening in your game, let me clarify: no.

replies.author: AsparagusOk8818
replies.body:
none of that solves the problem 

if you have instances capped at 20\~ players, and 100\~ players want to do an instance, then you have to simulate those instances. the fact you're running them in parallel doesn't save you; you need sufficient server-side infrastructure to run all 100\~ simulations while trusting literally no data from the players aside from inputs 

and how does this proposed solution solve botting at all? the most prevalent kind of cheating? a bot never tries to do a man in the middle attack - it plays by all of your rules and only gives inputs 

so you have to build a dedicated data center to run the cheat-proof MMO, and then it won't even be hardened against the most common form of cheat

replies.author: very_bad_programmer
replies.body: The AI told him it was a brilliant and novel idea

comments.author: NorberAbnott
comments.body: You will have to trust the player’s computer at some point, otherwise they won’t be able to do anything. Do you trust their inputs? If so, you will get bots. Do you trust their position updates? You’ll get teleporters. Do you have any bugs? They will cause you to trust data you didn’t mean to.
